atlas-lt.0110: A curricular internship under a three-way agreement is covered by a Lithuanian study permit; students of foreign universities need a D visa or an internship permit.
atlas-lt.0111: A voluntary internship is unpaid, for under-29s, two months at most with one host, and is no basis for a visa from abroad.
atlas-lt.0112: Permit to look for work or start a business after graduating
atlas-lt.0113: After a degree from a Lithuanian university: 12 months, not renewable, with the state fee waived once. A Lithuanian graduate hired within ten years skips the labour-market test.
atlas-lt.0114: €1,153 a month plus €1,153 for the return: €14,989
atlas-lt.0115: A three-year degree, or five years of experience (three in the last seven for ICT managers and specialists), and a contract of at least six months.
atlas-lt.0116: No quota and no labour-market test; you may start work once the application is accepted in MIGRIS, and family joins at once.
atlas-lt.0121: A full-time contract plus a matching qualification, a year of experience in the last three, or the national average wage. The yearly quota of 24,706 ran out on 7 September 2026; after that only higher salaries qualify.
atlas-lt.0122: Salary once the quota is used
atlas-lt.0123: €2,893.68 a month gross; €2,411.40 for listed professions
atlas-lt.0125: No change of employer in the first six months, and the permit is revoked if the job ends before a new employer is approved.
atlas-lt.0126: A hosting agreement with an accredited university or institute: no labour-market test, no quota, family at once; afterwards a 12-month permit to look for work.
atlas-lt.0127: A PhD stipend is free of income tax and social contributions, and full-time doctoral students get public health cover from the state.
atlas-lt.0128: Lithuania’s working-holiday agreements are only with Japan, Canada and New Zealand.
atlas-lt.0129: For Japanese and New Zealanders aged 18 to 30 and Canadians aged 18 to 35: a D visa for up to 12 months that can be converted in Lithuania into a work permit or Blue Card.
atlas-lt.0130: Up to 90 days in any 180, with no ordinary work.
atlas-lt.0131: Nothing to arrange in advance; if you will stay more than 3 months in six, you will apply for an EU residence certificate through the MIGRIS portal.
atlas-lt.0132: Applications filed abroad through the external provider VFS Global carry a €110 service fee on top of the state fee.
atlas-lt.0133: Declare your place of residence within 1 month of getting your residence document: online through Registrų centras with the owner’s electronic consent, or in person at the ward office (seniūnija) with a lease entered in the property register. The flat must have at least 7 m² per adult registered there (4 m² for students).
atlas-lt.0134: Apply in MIGRIS for the certificate of the EU citizen’s right of temporary residence, and collect it at the Migration Department.
atlas-lt.0135: Collect the plastic residence permit card at the Migration Department office you chose, where fingerprints are taken, or through VFS Global abroad.
atlas-lt.0136: Your residence document carries your 11-digit personal code (asmens kodas), yours for life and needed for health care, tax, work and utilities.
atlas-lt.0137: Employees are covered by compulsory public health insurance once the employer registers them with Sodra, which it must do before the first day of work.
atlas-lt.0138: If you are not employed, paying Sodra yourself does not give public cover and can cost you the permit: take private insurance of at least €30,000 for the whole stay.
atlas-lt.0139: Many newcomers start with Revolut Bank UAB, licensed in Lithuania with a Lithuanian IBAN, avoiding the €200 to €250 non-refundable onboarding fees of traditional banks.
atlas-lt.0140: With your personal code, activate Smart-ID or Mobile-ID, the standard digital ID for signing contracts and using MIGRIS, the tax office and Sodra.
atlas-lt.0141: A permit holder without valid health insurance can lose the permit, so keep cover in place between jobs.
atlas-lt.0142: There is no bridging status: apply while visa-free and still be waiting on day 91, and the application must be refused, with a removal order and a Schengen entry ban. Apply early or leave before day 90.
atlas-lt.0143: You must declare your address within a month, with at least 7 m² per adult. Many landlords refuse consent; write it into the lease. Bought fake addresses lead to revocation.
atlas-lt.0144: If you do not work, you cannot buy into public health insurance through Sodra: you need private cover of at least €30,000.
atlas-lt.0145: Criminal-record certificates are needed from every country you lived in for over six months in the last two years, apostilled and in sworn Lithuanian translation.
atlas-lt.0146: Since December 2024 VFS centres outside your own country turn ordinary applicants away; Blue Card applicants, researchers and students are exempt.
atlas-lt.0147: MIGRIS appointments for fingerprints are scarce in Vilnius; regional offices are often faster.
atlas-lt.0148: Since January 2026 foreign workers dealing with customers must speak basic Lithuanian; how checks are enforced is still unclear.
atlas-lt.0149: How long the extra restrictions on Russian and Belarusian citizens will last.
atlas-lt.0150: Banks charge new residents account-opening fees despite the right to a basic account.
